body:
### Summary

The cache holds both reusable artifacts and files that live processes need. A cache lock held by uv cannot protect those files after uv dies.

A local PEP 517 reproduction demonstrates this on macOS: kill only uv, then run plain `uv cache clean`. The backend remains alive, but its environment disappears and its next write fails with `ENOENT`. The removal loop merged in #22171 permits the same failure through prune. Another reproduction needs no signal: one parallel build fails, and uv removes another live backend's environment.

A possible architecture fix:

1. Put uv-owned execution workspaces outside `UV_CACHE_DIR`. This includes build sources, temporary environments, and reusable executable environments. Cache clean and prune remove reusable artifacts.
2. Give the child and its workspace one owner, with explicit async shutdown. Cancellation goes through that owner. It keeps the workspace through exit and output collection.
3. Make those workspaces independent of cache paths. Copy or clone package files, or hardlink immutable files. Avoid runtime dependency symlinks into the evictable cache. Create environments at their final path and reuse them there.

Completed build outputs enter the cache after the build completes. Old execution entries need conservative retention during migration.

Unknown process lifetime means keep the workspace. A dead parent, an unlocked lease, or direct-child exit cannot prove that every descendant stopped. Automatic recovery after crashes remains a separate problem. The tradeoff is retained workspaces after uncertain exits.

### Example

After parent-only `SIGKILL`, cache cleanup leaves the backend's workspace and imports usable. An error in another parallel build also preserves them. A detached descendant with closed output pipes retains its workspace.

The recorded reproductions cover macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with Python 3.14.7. Cache clean fails this requirement on uv 0.12.23. The prune reproduction used PR CI revision `013216c409a2ce74821f25d9d84ce0747a0301ba`. The proposed architecture has no implementation or Linux/Windows runtime validation yet.

Related to #22167, #18962, and #20116.

Codex helped prepare the reproductions and this proposal.
title: Separate runtime workspace ownership from cache cleanup
